about: Tests that fail on the local .NET 8 runner although Unity (Mono) is green. Each entry names the test and message fragments of the one failure explained here; a different failure of the same test is NOT covered and shows as a plain failure. Causes are described in README.md (Known differences).

unity_baseline.sdk_note: Packages/com.vrchat.worlds/Editor/Udon/UnityEditorTests (9 files, compiled and discovered once by hand on 2026-11-16: 191 cases); never built by this tool.

differences.explanation: Unity's Mono keeps the intermediates of a float expression in double precision, .NET rounds every float operation. TrySphereVolumeMm3(30 m) multiplies pi/6 * 30 * 30 * 30 in float: Mono rounds once (14137.1669921875, cap volume 14137166921728 mm3 <= Cap30Mm3, so the ball is exactly at the cap and reports 30 m); .NET rounds after each step (14137.16796875, cap volume 14137167970304 mm3 > Cap30Mm3), takes the cube-root branch and gets 30.0000019. With --continue-after-failure the next assertion (diameterA == diameterB) fails too, for the same reason: diameterB (4x the cap) is at the cap and exactly 30.

The ramp plane offset n.y*0.35 + n.z*z is computed in float. Strict float gives exactly 0 at the foot (ramp height 0.0, not strictly above the ground, so the ground wins: id 0); Mono's double intermediates leave 8e-10 (ramp height 9.2e-10 > 0, the ramp wins: id 500, which is what the test expects).

The test finds the lab MonoBehaviour by scanning the loaded assemblies; it lives in Assets/VRC_Katamari/Labs (Unity's Assembly-CSharp), which check.py does not compile, so the type is absent here. Not a behaviour difference; the test would need the engine anyway (JsonUtility, MonoBehaviour).
